done

The three classes now live in `src/click/params.py`, along with `batch` and `_check_iter`, which only they used. All three import paths give the same class objects. `from click.params import ...` works on its own, and so does `from click.core import ...`.

The test run shows 24 failures, all under `tests/test_utils` (the `echo_via_pager` ones), and 2604 passed. No other test fails. I didn't touch any tests. I didn't check whether those 24 also fail without my change.

- **Circular import:** `params.py` imports from `core.py`. So `core.py` can't import the classes at the top, and a lazy module-level `__getattr__` serves `Parameter`, `Option` and `Argument` for `from click.core import ...`. The few runtime `isinstance` checks inside `core.py` import them locally.
- **Other imports:** `__init__.py`, `decorators.py` and `shell_completion.py` now import the three classes from `.params`. I did not touch `parser.py`, `types.py` or `exceptions.py`, which still import them from `.core` under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
- **Cleanup:** I removed imports that became unused in both files. `ruff` isn't installed, so I found them with a crude script, not a linter.
